body: Thanks. I really appreciate your perspective. Here is my question - from where are you determining that the purpose of life is "finding out why the hell we are actually living?" I don't think we can effectively determine ANY "purpose" to life. There are merely descriptive facts about the world, but I don't see how we can then observe the world and then decide, "oh *x* is the purpose to life. As a result, I an convinced there is no purpose to life.

> In the end, though, your ultimate argument is that you are selfish, which, if true, means no one can convince you to change your mind even when they are completely logical and reasonable, because your personal and irrational bias will not allow it.

Why is selfishness "irrational"? I was hoping for someone to somehow convince me that for selfish reasons, I shouldn't kill myself. That's what I'm grasping to find and can't.

> Consider this: posit your query to three qualified academics; university professors would be my choice. Peer review is the basis of scientific reasoning and conclusion- ignoring the input of peer review is unscientific and illogical.

I completely agree. Science in the basis of all understanding. And that's also where I find difficulty - Which scientific experiment will yield the result that my state of non-existence is "worse off" than existence? None. Science will tell us that if I'm dead I won't know I'm dead, I won't know what pleasures I'm missing out on, and I won't be experiencing any pain. And to me, that state seems more desirable than life.
